Myth. "I need more leads."

Most businesses don't need more leads. They need to stop losing the ones they already paid for.

Missed calls. Slow replies. Quotes nobody followed up on.

Plug the leaks before you pay for more traffic.

Money move for today.

1. Open your call log and count the calls you missed last week.
2. Multiply by your average job.
3. Multiply by how often a caller actually books.

That's what voicemail cost you in one week. Most owners have never run this math. Run it once and you'll never ignore a ringing phone again.

Morgan Housel makes a point in The Psychology of Money that every owner should remember.

Wealth is what you don't see. It's the money you didn't spend.

In business that means the cheapest growth is the revenue you stop leaking, not the new revenue you chase.

Find one leak this week and plug it.

Myth check. Which one did you believe the longest?

A) Good work markets itself
B) Cheaper prices win more customers
C) I'll hire help once I can afford it
D) Customers hate talking to AI

Reply with your letter. I'll tell you what it's costing you.

Building in public, with real numbers.

My AI Front Desk costs $997 to set up and $297 a month. The first 3 clients get setup for $497 in exchange for an honest testimonial.

Why post my prices? Because hiding them wastes your time and mine.

Too high, too low, or fair? Tell me straight.

Myth. Discounts win deals.

Discounts win price shoppers, and price shoppers leave the second someone is cheaper.

Win on speed and certainty instead. Answer first, quote first, follow up first.

Nobody discounts their way to a great business.

Straight up, I'm here to make money, and I want you making more of it too.

I build AI that answers every call, texts back every missed one, follows up on every quote, and asks every customer for a Google review.

Want that running in your business? DM me MONEY and I'll show you exactly what it would catch for you.

Every unanswered call is a customer deciding who gets their money.

Make sure it's you.

I run my business with a team of AI bots.

One finds prospects. One drafts outreach. One writes content. One watches the website. One briefs me every morning.

None of them get paid. All of them clock in.

What would you hand to a bot first?

Steal my setup for a 10 minute money briefing.

1. Paste yesterday's unread emails into ChatGPT or Claude.
2. Ask it to sort them into money, problems, and noise.
3. Answer the money ones before 9 AM.

You start every day knowing where the cash is.

Robert Kiyosaki's simplest lesson in Rich Dad Poor Dad. An asset puts money in your pocket. A liability takes it out.

Run that test on your business tools. The software you pay for every month and never open is a liability. The system that books jobs while you sleep is an asset.

Cancel one liability today.

Builders, real question.

What's the one system in your business that makes you money while you're not looking?

If the answer is nothing, that's the next thing to build. Drop yours below.

Honest build update.

My own business line is answered by the AI I sell. Every call, nights and weekends included.

If I won't trust it with my own phone, I have no business selling it to you.

Would you let AI answer your business line? Yes or no.

The money is in the follow up, and almost nobody does it.

Pull up every quote you sent in the last 30 days. Text every one that went quiet. Today.

Tell me tomorrow how many replied.

Here's my offer, no fluff.

I'm taking 3 founding clients for my AI Front Desk. You get setup for $497 instead of $997, and I get an honest testimonial and a case study.

It answers every call, books the job, and texts back anyone you miss.

Want one of the 3 spots? DM me MONEY.

Hustle runs out. Systems don't.

Build the system.

Unpopular opinion. Your prices aren't too high. Your follow up is too slow.

People pay more to the business that answers first.

Speed is the cheapest thing you'll ever sell.

Prompt Friday. Copy this to find money you're leaving on the table.

"Here are my services and prices [paste them]. Act as a profit consultant. Show me 3 add ons or upgrades my customers would happily pay for, and write the one sentence my staff should say to offer each one."

One upsell line, said every time, adds up fast.

Chris Voss, the FBI negotiator behind Never Split the Difference, has a move for when a client says your price is too high.

Don't drop it. Ask "How am I supposed to do that?"

Then stay quiet. Most of the time they find the budget, or they show you what they'd actually pay.

Friday question.

What's the one price you know you should raise but haven't?

Tell me the service. I'll reply with how I'd raise it without losing the customer.

Second prompt for your Friday. This one gets you reviews.

"Write a short, friendly text asking a customer for a Google review after [the job]. Thank them for one specific thing, keep it under 300 characters, and include this link [your review link]."

Reviews are free advertising that never stops running.

If your business only makes money when you're in the room, you don't own a business. You own a job with extra stress.

Build one system this month that runs without you.

Two ways to work with me, both straight.

We run it. I set up your AI front desk and run it month to month, with the minutes, tuning, updates, and a monthly report.

You run it. You pay once, I build it in your own accounts, train your team, and hand you the keys.

Either way, every call gets answered. DM me MONEY and tell me which one fits.

Somewhere tonight a customer is calling a business.

The one that answers gets paid.

The best seller beats the best expert. Every time.

You can be the most skilled person in your trade and still lose to the one who calls back first and explains it better.

Skill gets you in the game. Selling gets you paid.

Use AI to rehearse your next sales call.

1. Tell ChatGPT or Claude to play a tough customer who thinks you're too expensive.
2. Make your pitch and let it push back hard.
3. Ask it to grade your answers and rewrite your weakest one.

Practice where it's free, so you don't learn on a real deal.

Dale Carnegie's whole book comes down to this. Talk about what the other person wants and show them how to get it.

Your customer doesn't want a roof, a website, or an AI system. They want to stop worrying, save time, and make money.

Sell that. The product is just how they get there.

Sales question for the room.

What's the objection you hear most?

A) Too expensive
B) Need to think about it
C) Need to ask my partner
D) Already have someone

Reply with your letter and I'll give you the line I'd use.

Chris Voss calls this labeling, and it saves deals.

When a customer goes quiet, say "It seems like something about this doesn't sit right with you."

Then wait. They'll tell you the real objection, and you can't answer an objection you never hear.

Nobody buys an AI receptionist.

They buy the job that would have gone to voicemail.

Sell the job, not the robot.

If your business lives on the phone, I'll do one thing for you free.

DM me MONEY and I'll work out what your missed calls are probably costing you, using your own numbers.

No pitch unless you ask for one.
Respect the customer's time and they'll respect your price.

Sunday truth. Busy isn't the same as profitable.

If you're slammed and still short on cash, the problem isn't effort. It's price, follow up, or work nobody is billing for.

Which one is it for you?

Sunday money audit, 15 minutes.

1. List every subscription your business pays for.
2. Mark the ones you actually used this week.
3. Cancel one you didn't.

Then ask AI for 3 tasks you did by hand this week that it could do. That's next week's time back.

Adam Grant's research in Give and Take shows givers end up at both the bottom and the top.

The ones at the top help generously and still guard their time.

In business that means give away real value, then make it easy to pay you for the rest.

Owners, honest question for your Sunday.

If your business made 20% more next month, where would the money come from?

More customers, higher prices, or fewer leaks? Your answer tells you what to fix first.

End of week build note.

This week I posted 8 times a day here. All of it written with AI, checked by me, and posted by a script on a schedule.

The point isn't to post more. It's to free my hours for the conversations that make money.

If you're in the replies, you're the reason I do it.

Money loves speed.

Answer fast. Quote fast. Follow up fast. Get paid fast.

The plain offer for the week ahead.

I build AI that answers your calls, books your jobs, follows up on your quotes, and asks for your reviews. I run it for you, or I build it in your accounts so you own it.

3 founding spots at $497 setup. When they're gone, they're gone.

DM me MONEY to grab one, or get my free review kit at evogencyglobal.com/free-review-kit

New week tomorrow.

Plug one leak. Raise one price. Answer every call.
